note: The lanes and the permission model for a Claude/Terry board. Terry dictated this lane by lane on 2026-08-18, in the shape he asked for: "I like that the perms are (in/out, actor, source/dest)." It lives outside the code because a rule change should be a data diff a person can read, and because `git log rules.json` then shows ONLY permission history rather than mixing it with page CSS. Every edge is declared TWICE, once from each end, and status.check_edges() refuses to let the halves disagree -- Terry reasons one lane at a time, so the table is written the way he thinks and the machine catches what that costs.

lanes.label: Backlog
lanes.note: Someday. Terry's queue, and the only lane Claude may CREATE in besides Ready for Claude. Terry gained create here on 2026-08-19 for the + button in the lane header (card #0038). He could always ADD a card -- by asking Claude to run the CLI -- so this grants him the keystroke rather than the power.

needs_terry_action.note: Claude may take a backlog card to Needs Terry and NOWHERE else. Terry, 2026-08-18: "that way if I comment in backlog, you can reply with a clarify question and move it to Needs Terry." The edge names its destination, so raising a question is expressible without granting Claude any power to advance its own queue.

ready_for_claude.note: Terry promotes from the backlog, and that is what makes the queue his. CLAUDE HAS THIS EDGE AND MUST NOT USE IT UNSOLICITED. Terry, 2026-08-19: "If something changes on a ticket in backlog that suddenly makes it eligible for work, Terry can grant *per-ticket* permission to move from backlog to RFW. Note that claude MUST NOT move out of backlog until/unless Terry gives explicit guidance for one specific ticket." The grant is PER TICKET and verbal; the table cannot express that, so the restraint lives in CLAUDE.md and ORIENTATION.md. A standing permission read off this row alone would let Claude fill its own queue, which is the one thing every other edge here is shaped to prevent.

in_progress.note: Terry starting something straight out of his own queue. Claude has no such edge and MUST NOT gain one -- promotion out of the backlog is what makes the queue his.

lanes.label: Ready for Claude
lanes.note: Do this next, in priority order. Terry fills it; Claude empties it. CREATING here is not PROMOTING here -- Claude files a card he just asked for in chat, but only Terry moves one in from the backlog, so Claude can never advance its own queue. Terry gained create here on 2026-08-19 for the + button (card #0038). CREATING here is still not PROMOTING here: the create right and the backlog->ready_for_claude edge are separate entries, and Claude has the first unconditionally and the second only per-ticket.

The grant is PER TICKET and verbal; the table cannot express that, so the restraint lives in CLAUDE.md and ORIENTATION.md. lanes.label: In progress
lanes.note: Being worked now. Claude's lane end to end.

ready_for_claude.note: Terry started it, then decided Claude should carry it. This is the one way a card reaches Ready for Claude from work already under way, and it is Terry's alone for the same reason every other entry to that lane is.

lanes.label: Needs Terry
lanes.note: Claude is STOPPED until Terry answers. His definition: "that's 'need a judgement call'." Distinct from blocked, where nobody can act, and from review, where the work is done and only a tick is missing.

backlog.note: Answered, but not soup yet. "I may post a reply and realize that card is not yet soup and goes to backlog for now." Answering and prioritizing are different acts, and one exit would have forced him to queue work he only meant to unblock.

ready_for_claude.note: Answered, go. His words: "I'll move there when I feel I've unblocked you."

lanes.label: Blocked
lanes.note: NEITHER of us can move it. Terry's example: "awaiting license key." MUST NOT be used for "waiting on a decision" -- that is needs_terry_action -- and MUST NOT be used for "hard".

ready_for_claude.note: Unblocked, requeue. This edge is why Blocked is NOT a pure Claude lane, which the cross-check revealed rather than anyone noticing.

lanes.label: Ready for review
lanes.note: Claude believes it is done and is waiting on a signoff. This is as far as Claude may take anything.

completed.note: THE SIGNOFF, and the single edge Claude has no actor on. "Claude must not sign off its own work" is a missing table entry rather than a rule somebody remembers. It exists because Claude marked its own work complete twice on 2026-08-18 and was wrong both times.

in_progress.note: Claude pulling back work it decides is not actually finished. "claude can pull BACK from ready for terry review but Terry is only one that is ready to review out -> completed."

lanes.label: Completed
lanes.note: Terminal. An empty `out` IS append-only, enforced by the same rule as everything else rather than by a special flag.

ready_for_review.note: The only way in, and only Terry may take it.
